findings.summary: The plan drops the `N)` and `N.` part forms the accepted reading designed for, so a plain numbered list of parts is never checked.
findings.evidence: The reading says to 'extract parts from lines or clauses that start with (N), N) or N.'. Plan Decision 2 takes only `(N)` markers plus bullets under an `Acceptance:` heading. It rejects 'Treat every bullet or numbered line of a request as a part'. So a request written as '1. add X\n2. add Y\n3. add Z' with no Acceptance heading gives no parts, and a reading that defers item 3 to a follow-up is still accepted. is_bullet (reading.rs:1992) already treats '1. ' lines as explicit request items for `athena plan`. A numbered list is the most common way to write explicit parts, so this is the root-cause class left open, not a rare edge. One introspection also names lettered parts, (a) (b) (c). Fix: Also take line-start `N.` and `N)` markers as parts, with the same rule already used for `(N)`: they must run 1, 2, 3... from 1, there must be at least two, and each must hold a distinctive word. That still keeps stray single numbers and quoted runs out. Either add `(a)`/`a)` lettered runs under the same rule, or say in the plan why they are left out. Add a demonstration under criterion 2 or 3: a '1./2./3.' request whose reading defers item 3 is refused.
findings.location: Plan Decision 2 (parts parser) vs. the accepted reading's Design assumption

findings.summary: Applied as written, the plan's stem rules do not let a typical criterion cover the standard Steward bullet, which contradicts the plan's own demonstration and points to false refusals on every Steward request.
findings.evidence: Bullet: 'A test fails without the change and passes with it, for the cause and not only for one job'. Under Decision 3: test, fail, pass, with, only and job are stop words. 'change' strips its trailing e to 'chang', which matches the stop entry 'change' only if the stop list is checked before stemming, and the plan does not say when. 'without' is not a stop word and is kept. 'cause' becomes 'caus'. So the bullet's stems are about {without, caus} plus maybe {chang}, and it needs 2 shared. The plan's 'typical' criterion, 'a test that fails before the change', yields {befor, chang} at most, so it shares 0 or 1 stems and is refused. This job's own accepted criterion 1 ('fails on the code before the change and passes after it') would be refused the same way. Every Steward request carries this bullet, and a second refusal fails the request (briefs.rs:1588-1590), so a stop list built by hand and an unstated stemming order are a crude basis for the gate. Fix: Define the stop list as stems by passing it through `stems` itself, so 'change' and 'chang' cannot disagree. Add common function words of four or more letters (without, before, after, into, also, about, them, then, there, where, other). Trace the three standard Steward bullets against the plan's own example criteria by hand in the plan, and change the threshold until they pass. For example, need = 1 when a part has three or fewer stems. Or treat a criterion that quotes most of the bullet as covering it. State the result in the Criterion 6 (ii) demonstration.
findings.location: Plan Decision 3 (stems / stop list) and the Criterion 6 demonstration (ii), Steward-bullet hand-check

findings.summary: An affirmative pattern inside a quoted or reported sentence still exempts the part.
findings.evidence: Only negation words are checked. A retry request such as 'the earlier reading said (3) is a follow-up; that was wrong' contains '(3) is a follow-up' with no negation before it, so part (3) is exempt. Complaint-style requests of exactly this kind are what this failure class produces. Fix: Refuse the exemption when the sentence that holds the pattern also has a reporting or complaint cue (said, claimed, wrongly, wrong, the reading, the earlier, rejected). Or count only patterns whose subject is the part label at the start of a clause. Add this case to the still-refused tests for criterion 3.

findings.summary: Criterion 1 says the test uses the 'real request text' of job 20261029-084645-sza7, but the plan rebuilds it from the brief.
findings.evidence: A Grep of the snapshot for 'sza7' finds nothing, and records/ is absent. The plan says this in its open questions. Fix: Have the test comment and the change description state plainly that the text is rebuilt from the brief, so the verifier does not count the test as a failed criterion.

summary: I read reading.rs (is_bullet and request_text_acceptance at 1992-2008, check_reading_acceptance at 2599, check_governance_coverage at 2674) and briefs.rs (READING_RULES at 1557, the rule-section test at 3172). The plan fixes the right place. check_reading_acceptance is the gate every reading passes, and the plan's call site, early return and refusal message follow check_governance_coverage. Its demonstrations call the real gate and use the existing scoped_reading helper. The briefs.rs change fits the rule-section test: one more line of about 190 bytes keeps the section under its 2400-byte cap, by my estimate, not a measurement. I found two soundness problems. First, the parser checks only `(N)` markers and Acceptance bullets. That drops the `N.` and `N)` numbered parts the accepted reading designed for, so a plain numbered request still lets the reader defer a part. Second, the stem rules as specified do not let a typical criterion cover the standard Steward bullet 'A test fails without the change…'. The stop list is applied in an unstated order, 'without' is not in it, and two shared stems are required. This contradicts the plan's own Criterion 6 hand-check and puts false refusals on the most common request shape. Also minor: an affirmative pattern inside a quoted complaint still exempts the part. Both major findings can be fixed inside the plan, so the verdict is revise.
